Obrtrol / Gerudaghot (Obrtrol Z17 → Gerudaghot Z74)

Region (English scoring-table region): Wescann / Gerudia.

In one sentence: Lead the northern fjord trolls through encirclement to reclaim their ancestral land and build a Gerudian empire from ancient giant relics; the powerful restoration story also carries slave labour and the destruction of cities.

Story: High ｜ Mission-tree length: Very long (55 direct missions across the continuous Z17 and Z74 campaign) ｜ Mission-tree update: Local file modified 7 September 2026, supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 ｜ Uniqueness: High ｜ Prison-like opening: Medium-high (opening survival and later regional prosperity/university gates) ｜ Early pressure: Extreme (northern isolation and southern threats) ｜ Expansion capacity: Very high (formation grants Gerudian claims)

The Last Troll Land in the North

The current English localisation distinguishes Z17 as Obrtrol and Z74 as Gerudaghot. In 1444 the player starts as Z17: current province history confirms nine provinces, while the country history gives Fjord Troll culture, Mountain Watchers faith, a settled tribal reform, and the Northern Troll technology group. The capital is province 995, and the opening ruler is Svala “the Crusher” Hardrock, with Barg as heir. Z74 has a country-history file, but it is not the 1444 starting country here; it is formed through Obrtrol's missions.

Obrtrol's ancient origin appears mainly as a Troll ancestral tradition in the current mission narrative: the ancient giants built caves, forges, and towers in the north and then disappeared; the Fjord Trolls believe they inherited the land and relics, and view human settlement as the theft of their homeland. The offline English Wiki also describes them as servants of the Frost Giants who guarded the north after the giants declined and were later driven back into the mountains by united human tribes; “the trolls were created by the Frost Giants” is presented there as a disputed claim. The Wiki's ancient chronology contains ordering contradictions, so only the historical pattern is used here, not a precise ancient year. The opening pressure is concrete: the northern tribes must be integrated, southern human countries are strong enemies, and Obrtrol lacks a deep economic hinterland and has not rebuilt the giant sites. Older player guides often say to use winter mountains and forts to stop early attacks; that is version-bound experience, not a scripted guarantee that a declaration will occur on a particular day.

Survive First, Then Reclaim Gerud

The first half of the missions intertwines war, tribal organization, and capital construction. You first contest the fjords with Bjarnrík and the countries of Gerudia, then reclaim Urviksten's giant forge, repair the capital and ancient fortress, and contact forest trolls and shamans. Winning wars is not enough: the missions also require capital development, a mage tower, and rebuilding the connections to the ancient relics. Strong Troll armies help, but cannot replace economic and construction gates.

The key mission “Reclaim the Legacy of Gerud” requires three related branches to be complete, peace, and control of two core provinces. If Z74 does not exist, it changes Z17 into Gerudaghot, changes the government to monarchy, raises the government rank, adds the Northern Guardians reform, and replaces the non-generic missions; without custom ideas, it also triggers an idea conversion. If Z74 already exists, the mission gives money only and cannot force a second formation. This is a real change of national form, not merely a striking new name for the old country. There are 25 shared missions before and after formation, plus 30 Z74-specific missions; the total is 55 direct missions, not 55 new missions all stacked after formation.

Gerudaghot: Mammoths, Runes, and Rule of the North

The post-formation goals go beyond “drive out the humans.” One line requires control of Gerudia, establishment of cores, restoration of prosperity across the region, and even universities and public schools in several provinces. Another trains mammoths, manages northern roads and mineral resources, and turns ancient giant palaces, runes, and treasures into tools of rule. The choice of giant relics is driven by the later event chain, not a reward taken casually at the start. The holy sites and blessings of the Mountain Watchers are also tied to this restoration story. Pushing farther north brings contact with forest trolls, grey orcs, and ogres; events allow grey-orc culture to be accepted and can grant ogre homelands and generous taxation. This gives the empire the appearance of a “giant kindred community,” but it is not equally open to every sapient people.

That is the campaign's sharpest contradiction. Z17's capital province history already contains an oppressed human minority; the prequel missions lower tolerance of humans, and the narrative puts captured human slave labour into city construction. Later Z74 missions add permanent “Slave Mine” modifiers in several mining areas and further lower human tolerance. Later Amldihr missions actively reduce the development of four Dwarven holds, create severe devastation, and leave long-term ruin modifiers. Accepting grey orcs, helping ogres, and opening public schools are real countervailing elements, but they do not cancel institutional harm to humans and Dwarves. The mission tree's “restoration” is a player-driven future; it does not mean that 1444 Obrtrol already possesses a giant empire or has completed these abuses.

Personality and Recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 91/100 ｜ Authoritarianism 78/100 ｜ Magic ↔ Artifice 76/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 55/100) ｜ Pluralism 36/100. The phases are: northern tribal survival (Expansion 73, Authoritarianism 60, magic/artifice intensity 26) → the Gerudaghot giant empire (Expansion 94, Authoritarianism 83, magic/artifice intensity 58). Conquest, monarchization, and the giant inheritance dominate; runes, shamans, and mountain blessings matter, but do not eclipse military restoration. Pluralism is not extremely low because grey-orc and ogre acceptance and settlement are available, but human slave institutions and the destruction of Dwarven holds place clear limits on that openness.

The v2.1 value assessment is Evil (29/100), with a worsening trajectory. The phases are: tribal survival and existing human oppression (Neutral 40/100) → institutional slave mines and the destruction of Dwarven holds (Evil 20/100). The score is not because the country is Troll, expansionist, or monarchical; it is because of forced labour imposed on humans, slave mines, and deliberate destruction of Dwarven cities. Public works and protection of some groups provide limited public benefit and recognition of personhood, but do not outweigh the main harms. This suits players who want a hard opening, strong Troll armies, ancient giant relics, and a long northern-empire campaign; it is a poor fit for players who dislike early defensive wars, later regional prosperity/university gates, or a dark narrative supported by slave labour and reprisal. Evidence layers and old-version community experience are recorded on the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

Native English national-idea names and descriptions are reproduced below with the inherited effect displays. Traditions apply when this set is adopted; its seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Alternative sets and successor ideas do not automatically stack. Descriptions may recount history or depict future ideals, not events already completed in 1444. Native English wording is reused rather than back-translating embellished Chinese localisation. Inherited display-unit assumptions remain unverified; this translation does not correct source data.

Obrtrol (Z17) — Frost Troll Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        tag = Z17
    }

Traditions: Frost Troll Traditions

Effects: Ruler culture advisor cost: -15%; Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 1: Discover that Oceans are Not Scary

In daring move by matriarch, Trollkind discovered oceans are not dangerous by jumping in water. Trollkind thought oceans were deadly because Giant ancestors drowned because of bad dragons. Now Trollkind know big water not bad, and matriarch smart and good leader.

Effects: Horde unity: +1; Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Horde unity: +1.

Idea 2: Bolster the Mountain Holds

Mountain caves attacked by bad humans recently. Other day good idea from Bhagrat, put big stones around cave entrance like old Giant fortress. Humans have trouble getting in Troll cave now.

Effects: Fort defense: +15%.

Idea 3: Crush the Puny Humans

Obrtrol has many puny human slaves that Troll treat too well. Humans don't appreciate our hospitality. Troll matriarch made new Law Stones to beat bad slaves with if they misbehave.

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Idea 4: Reconsider Inferiority of Human Ideas

Trollkind decide that humans dumb, but some of their ideas not bad. With this decision Trollkind adopt strange new things from humankind that we can use against them.

Effects: Idea cost: -10%.

Idea 5: Mammoth-Driven Artillery

With new things from humans Trollkind came up with good idea, better than humans'. Trollkind drive big boom devices with mammoths to take down pesky human walls.

Effects: Siege ability: +10%.

Idea 6: Refine Troll Elite Culture

Dumb humans laugh at glorious Trollkind culture. Troll culture is far superior to theirs, for Trolls have good fashion and cuisine, like mammoth fur hides and roast human. Maybe is time for Trolls to wear human clothing, at least the ones with the shiny objects on them, and the furry ones.

Effects: Prestige: +1.

Idea 7: Human Diet Good for Troll Skin

When Trollkind conquer human lands, we find new interesting foods. Meat is the best, but humans grow strange plants that taste yummy too. Brightest minds of Troll society discovered that eating a balanced diet leads to good healthy Trolls, and good healthy Trolls are good at smashing humans.

Effects: Army morale: +10%.

Ambition: Frost Troll Ambition

Effects: Discipline: +5%.

Gerudaghot (Z74) — Gerudaghot Ideas

Applicable condition; separate alternative, not a stacked set:

    trigger = {
        tag = Z74
    }

Traditions: Gerudaghot Traditions

Effects: Leader land shock: +1; Discipline: +5%.

Idea 1: Until the Stones Grow

When they see the mountains of old The hearts of men grow cold Not one inch of land Will have a turn of hand Gerudaghot, Gerudaghot!

Through the ice Their armies will feel the vice Until the stones grow Not one knee will bow Gerudaghot, Gerudaghot!

-Gerudaghot marching song, inscribed by Chronicler Oxtir Troog (1704)

Effects: Fort defense: +15%; Hostile Attrition: +100%.

Idea 2: Mammoth Boom

The destruction of the humans has restored the order that once ruled everything. The natural order that saw it fit for giants to rule is back and here to stay, with the leftover tracks of Gerudian farmland becoming good eating for the mammoths that once roamed the land. The news of their return has spread across the continent, and has piqued the interest of puny humans looking to buy furs and tusks only we can provide.

Effects: Global trade power: +10%; Cavalry recruitment cost: -10%.

Idea 3: Slave Mines of Dalr

The mines of Dalrfjäll are of extreme importance to our new empire and our future plans. These caves are worked by humans, meatbags slaving away in the mines to earn their right to eat and sleep, providing us with the materials we need to continue our wars while they get our protection. But recently we've heard reports of humans becoming overstressed and rather... unsavory. Because of this, we changed the system of labor used in the mines, providing the wimpy little meatbags with proper schedules of work, ensuring they work good and grumble less.

Effects: Production efficiency: +10%.

Idea 4: Geruds Chosen

Gerud was the Frost Giant that ruled over the land eleven thousand years ago. The frost giants made us to protect them against any outsiders who dare approach the cold towers of the north. Every man, woman and child of Gerudaghot knows that defending the north is what we must do. By marking our warriors with the runes of the frost king we can remind them that we are the chosen ones that will protect the north until the end of days!

Effects: Army morale: +15%.

Idea 5: The Ordning

The world operates under a simple principle: the big rule over the small, and the small suck it up and do what we say. Problem is, the puny humans and their stinky allies found ways to turn our weaknesses against us, disrupting the natural balance of the world. Even now, as we rule over a land gained through our superiority, there are still those dumb enough to challenge our right to rule over them like the bugs they are. The discovery of the frost towers left by the giants here millennia ago have proven our beliefs beyond any shadow of a doubt, and has given us a greater, more concrete mandate that We are the Giant's chosen!

Effects: Stability cost modifier: -20%.

Idea 6: Nifltrolleri

The cold cannot hurt a troll, neither can the swords or sledgehammers of the dumb soldiers we've faced over the years. But with time the secret of our weakness to fire and acid became widespread, especially in this era of black powder and cannonballs. By calling on the power of the runes, we can bring the freezing cold with us and have our armies wear it like a moving blizzard, freezing bullets and turning any warriors willing to fight us into tasty meatsicles.

Effects: fire_damage_received：-10%.

Idea 7: Recipes of Every Race

Nothing is more legendary than the hunger of us trolls, whether it be the smallest troll child or the greatest of warchiefs, our love of a good meal is universal, and it shows in our recipes. Our contact with other races has greatly expanded our culinary palate, and we appreciate their contributions in the expansion of troll culinary culture, whether it be in stews, mashes, or puddings. With choices like these, no troll in our empire will be left wanting!

Effects: National unrest: -2.

Ambition: Gerudaghot Ambition

Effects: Core-creation cost: -15%.
